title: Comparing Mass Using a Balance
introduction: Explore comparing mass using a balance using everyday examples.
definition: A balance compares masses. When an object balances three identical weights, its mass equals three of those units. Use equal reference weights for comparison.

visuals.label: Balanced masses
visuals.description: One object balances three equal blocks.
visuals.alt: Balanced masses — One object balances three equal blocks.

examples.question: A toy balances four equal blocks.
steps: Its mass equals four block masses.

exercises.question: An apple balances 3 blocks. Mass in blocks?
exercises.solution: The balance is level with three equal blocks, so the apple has the same mass as 3 blocks.

exercises.question: Two objects balance 5 and 2 blocks. Heavier object's block count?
exercises.solution: 5 > 2, so the object balancing 5 equal blocks is heavier.

exercises.question: If both pans balance, are their masses equal? yes/no
exercises.solution: A level balance means the two pans have equal mass.

exercises.question: Two objects each balance 2 blocks. Combined mass?
A bag balances 6 blocks; remove an amount equal to 2 blocks. Remaining?

summary: A balance compares masses. When an object balances three identical weights, its mass equals three of those units. Use equal reference weights for comparison.
